messages:
carmen: Heads-up — we're seeing p99 token latency regressions (~120ms -> ~420ms) for some inference pods in eastus-2 since ~02:15 UTC. Rallying here to triage.

carmen: Metrics show an increase in east-west retransmits and a small spike in packet loss between gpu-node-03 and gpu-node-17. Not a whole-network outage but correlated with the SLO blips.

irene: Any recent infra changes in eastus-2? kernel, NIC firmware, or qdisc rollout?

sam: I rolled a small traffic-shaping tweak last night to add a conservative egress policy for noisy tenants — service: infra/egress-holdback. It added an htb parent + fq_codel child on bond0 on a subset of hosts.

carmen: Can you paste the tc qdisc dump from one affected host?

sam: Sure — from gpu-node-03:
```
# tc -s qdisc show dev bond0
qdisc htb 1: root refcnt 2 r2q 10 default 30 direct_packets_stat 0
 Sent 123456789 bytes  packets 987654
 qdisc fq_codel 10: parent 1:1 limit 10240 flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms ecn
 Sent 9876543 bytes  packets 87654
```

irene: fq_codel target/interval look defaulty. But htb classes?

sam: The BRANCH introduced a class with rate 500mbit and ceil 1gbit for tenant burst isolation — I figured it was safe.

nate: I ran iperf between the two nodes with 1M small UDP flows and saw ~0.6% packet loss and higher jitter when tc is enabled. When I disable the qdisc on the NIC, packet loss goes to 0.02% and latency stabilizes.

carmen: Interesting — could this be a bad interaction with RDMA (RoCE) path negotiation? I saw some RoCE fallback events in dmesg on gpu-node-17 around the time of the spike.

irene: Post dmesg excerpt?

sam: dmesg shows:
```
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: RoCE: link up, neg MTU 1500
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: RoCE: port 1: peer negotiated non-jumbo frames, falling back to TCP transport for smp group
```

nate: That peer negotiation line stood out to me. We run jumbo (9000) on the RDMA fabric normally. If fq_codel/hastle reduced packet sizes or caused fragmentation, negotiation could fail and force TCP fallback, which hurts latency for small RPCs.

carmen: Confirmed: ethtool -k on gpu-node-17 shows GSO/TSO momentarily disabled by the qdisc stack after some bursts.

irene: Ok so chain looks like: tc change applied -> fq_codel minute-level queuing -> RDMA peer says mtu mismatch/fallback -> increased TCP flows -> higher p99 RPC latency.

sam: I can revert the egress-holdback unit on the targeted hosts. Quick rollback should restore previous tc configuration.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4470 - eastus-2 inference p99 latency bump. Owner: eng-infra.

carmen: Please revert on the 6 affected hosts (gpu-node-03, -06, -17, -22, -28, -31). Sam — can you push a revert?

sam: Revert in flight. Running: systemctl stop egress-holdback && tc qdisc del dev bond0 root || true

sam: Reapply checks: iperf UDP small flows now show packet loss ~0.03% and latency back to baseline.

nate: Verified from the other side: RoCE link shows MTU 9000 negotiated again and no fallback messages in dmesg for the last 5m.

icr (carmen): Can we make the rollout safer? Ideas: dry-run on non-RDMA hosts, explicit RDMA-aware profile, or gate the qdisc by NIC tag.

irene: Also add a canary test in preflight that runs tiny RDMA handshake + iperf small-packet check before applying. If it fails, auto-rollback.

sam: I'll open a PR to change the systemd unit to include a preflight probe and to exclude hosts with mlx5 devices or where ethtool reports RDMA enabled. Link: https://github.com/redwood-infra/ops/commit/af3b9c2 (wip)

carmen: Good. Also, we should update runbook: include a checklist for MTU negotiation and GSO/TSO checks after qdisc changes.

nate: One more note — cost/throughput tradeoff: fq_codel reduced tenant burst tails but we can't accept SLO regressions for inference. For now revert; we'll model tail impact in perf lab.

ops-bot: Update: INC-2026-4470 severity: medium -> mitigated at 1890012399. Resolution note: egress-holdback rollout reverted on affected hosts; follow-up PR opened.

carmen: Thanks all — monitoring for 30m then close. :thumbsup:
